Senses.Explanation: Deliberation is repeatedly said not to reach the matter, while Yaoshan’s marked reply speaks of thinking what does not think; both claims remain attributed without adding an outside disciplinary frame. The exact rows retain their separate speakers, narrators, participants, and quoted layers; no single deployment is made to resolve all others.

Gathering the mind is the proposed finite action of collecting, drawing in, or holding in the mind. Chan records both give that action concrete work and challenge whether the wording has any stable basis: the tension belongs in the definition rather than being resolved into a system. The phrase occurs 137 times in 71 allowlisted texts. Asked to ‘show the way of gathering the mind’ (示攝心之法), Chaozong Tongren answers, ‘sit still for one stick of incense’ (靜坐一爐香), but immediately calls this ‘a fine saying’ and warns that it must not be misunderstood (好箇話頭，只是不得錯會). In a separate verse requested on the term, Chaozong says, ‘the myriad things are brightly clear—what thought and what consideration? If you intend to gather the mind, there is no basis to rely on. I now write these words for you; just this is the place of gathering the mind’ (萬法朗然，何思何慮？擬欲攝心，無本可據……只此便是攝心處).
Senses.Note: In the Extended Record of Yongjue Yuanxian, Yongjue quotes "gathering the mind is called restraint" (攝心名戒), then challenges it point by point: "what thing is mind that it can be gathered? What thing is gathering that it can gather mind? Water does not wash water" (心是何物而可攝？攝又是何物而可攝心？水不洗水). Yongming Yanshou's Source-Mirror Record states that before reaching its stated gate, "saying right makes wrong; gathering the mind is still an error" (說是成非，攝心猶錯). Shiwu Qinggong's community verse retains the ordinary finite action by listing chanting and "gathering the mind to drive off sleep" (攝心除睡). Counted forms include "gathering the mind is called restraint" (攝心名戒, two occurrences in two texts), "gather the mind to drive off sleep" (攝心除睡, two in two), "the way of gathering the mind" (攝心之法, one), "place of gathering the mind" (攝心處, one), and "gather the mind and illuminate within" (攝心內照, three in three). The entry records the action and the texts' own challenges without resolving those challenges into an external system.
